summary: Runtime request-outcome metric emitter, deterministic SLO burn exercise model, and Prometheus adapter coverage for backbone microservices observability/backpressure drills.
claim_boundary: In-process runtime metrics exercise and Prometheus reference adapter coverage only. This slice emits canonical counters/gauges through the existing HyperscalerMetrics trait and computes deterministic SLO burn-rate exercise reports. It does not add a Rust OpenTelemetry SDK/OTLP exporter, deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector, fire live Prometheus/Alertmanager alerts, or prove production backpressure behavior under load.

facets.F1_simplicity: A default trait method maps one RequestTelemetryOutcome into existing canonical metric families, avoiding per-service counter fan-out logic.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The slice adds pre-prod drill evidence for success, 429 backpressure, 5xx, circuit-open, retry-budget exhaustion, and integer SLO burn-rate thresholds before live cloud integration.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover invalid status codes, empty tenant/capability labels, zero-traffic SLO math, fast/slow burn triggering, Prometheus counter/gauge values, and CI package-matrix consistency.
facets.F5_quality: Focused metrics tests, broad 34-package backbone cargo check/test/clippy/fmt, Jenkins matrix validation, governance gates, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F7_security_privacy: Metric labels stay low-cardinality: microservice is bound at adapter construction, tenant_id is only used for 429 counters, and request bodies/principals/raw paths are never added to metric names.
facets.F11_observability: Runtime outcomes now produce request_total, request_success_total, responses_total, responses_429_total, responses_5xx_total, capability_circuit_state, and capability_retry_budget_exhausted_total observations in the Prometheus reference adapter. Live OpenTelemetry export remains pending.
